title: Ferron-driven motion of non-collinear ferroelectric domain walls
authors: Huanhuan Yang, Gerrit E. W. Bauer
abstract: We study the propagation of ferrons, the quanta of electric polarization waves, through a ferroelectric texture. We predict by analytic and numerical calculations that a $90^\circ$ domain wall (DW) operates as a beam splitter of longitudinal ferron and transverse optical phonon modes. An associated momentum-flux imbalance leads to forces that drive DW motion. In the weak-anisotropy limit, the DW becomes a rotating texture with nearly fixed-modulus, whose low-energy dynamics is described by a sine-Gordon equation. A ferron source then attracts the DW through a damping-induced force. Both driving forces scale linearly with incident wave intensity. Our results uncover qualitatively different routes to driven ferroelectric DW motion enabled by the vector nature of the polarization and offer functionalities for THz ferroelectric devices.
summary: This paper theoretically models how ferroelectric domain walls move when excited by electric polarization waves (ferrons). It shows that the non-collinear nature of the wall allows for a measurable driving force due to mode conversion, which scales with input intensity. This mechanism offers pathways for controlling DW motion for potential THz device applications.
main_problem: The study investigates the motion of non-collinear ferroelectric domain walls (DWs) when driven by the propagation of ferrons, the quanta of electric polarization waves.
main_result: The non-collinear nature of the DW allows for a finite driving force ($\Delta J_P$) via mode conversion, which scales linearly with incident wave intensity, enabling THz device functionalities.
method: The authors employ analytic and numerical calculations, linearizing the Landau-Khalatnikov-Tani (LKT) equations and using a collective-coordinate ansatz for the DW center.
model_or_system: The system models ferroelectric materials with $90^\circ$ domain walls, governed by the Ginzburg-Landau-Devonshire free energy functional. The dynamics are analyzed by treating the DW motion as a response to momentum-flux imbalances from incident ferrons.
key_observables: Momentum-flux imbalance ($\Delta J_P$), DW center dynamics ($\ddot{U}$), transmission amplitude ratio ($\chi_\parallel(k)$), and source-seeking velocity ($\dot{U}_{	ext{sat}}$).
important_parameters: Weak-anisotropy limit ($\kappa 	o 1+$), incident wave intensity, and the damping coefficient ($\Gamma_{	ext{DW}}$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the lowest-order collective-coordinate ansatz for the DW profile and assumes linear response to the ferron current.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate $90^\circ$ DW profiles in different anisotropy regimes, dispersion relations showing mode splitting, and time-series data demonstrating DW velocity driven by ferron intensity.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the physical mechanism where the DW acts as a beam splitter for ferron/phonon modes, leading to a driving force ($\Delta J_P$). It then analyzes the dynamics in the weak-anisotropy limit, showing both momentum-transfer driven motion and a separate source-seeking motion driven by dissipation-induced gradient forces.
why_interesting: The work connects fundamental concepts of wave propagation (beam splitting, mode conversion) in ferroelectrics to macroscopic dynamics (DW motion), which is relevant for understanding energy dissipation and control in solid-state quantum devices.
